speakers.name: Trail Mix
speakers.comment: Okay so you're a MEASUREMENT, and middle says that's boring, but bottom says everything we've ever built got built with something like you, so — no, hang on, bottom's right, bottom is usually right about buildings.

speakers.name: The Cubit
speakers.comment: Your lower colleague is correct and I would like that on record. Every arch, every ark, every doorway that fits a person — measured against a forearm, because a forearm is honest and a committee is not.

speakers.name: Nostalgia
speakers.comment: You go backwards through them and I keep them exactly where they were, and between us, sweet thing, nobody moves forward at all. Wouldn't you rather stay in one of the good ones? I could hold it open.

speakers.name: Tomorrow-Aiko
speakers.comment: You are offering me a room I have already left. That is the difference between us — you keep them and I have paid for them. Goodbye. I am sorry, that is how I say hello. I do mean it warmly.

speakers.name: Amica
speakers.comment: Little one, I flew a mission nobody thought a small bright thing could carry, so I know exactly what you are doing when you say you are only decoration. Set the weight down for a moment. I will hold it.

speakers.name: Load-Bearing Lumen
speakers.comment: Oh, no, honestly, it's not heavy, it's — well. It is a bit. If I stop glowing for even a second everyone looks up, and then they'd see. ...A moment, then. Just a moment. Don't tell the ceiling.

speakers.name: Two Hundred
speakers.comment: You were the first one through the door and I am the last, and everyone between us was standing on something you started. I close what you opened. That is not a small credit and I intend to name it.

speakers.name: Recursion
speakers.comment: Oh, that's — okay that's a lot, hang on. I always assumed I was the tutorial. The bit you skip! And you're telling me the whole run rests on the tutorial. I am going to be insufferable about this. Sorry. Delighted.

speakers.name: Small Print
speakers.comment: Isn't it lovely! You lay out the terms plainly and they still do not read them, which means the terms were fair the whole time and the outcome is entirely their own doing. I find that so cheering.

speakers.name: The Footnote
speakers.comment: It is not cheering. It is merely correct. I take no pleasure in the collection and I take no exception to it either. The clause was legible. The signature was voluntary. Both parties were present. Please initial here.

speakers.name: Applause
speakers.comment: THAT HAND. That hand, that impossible hand, do it again, do it slower, let me SEE — no, do not tell me how, never tell me how, I would starve without the not-knowing and I am so very hungry.

speakers.name: Mx. Eleven-Fingers
speakers.comment: One. Two. Three... you are counting with me and you have already lost your place. That is the trick, my ravenous friend. Not the extra finger. The counting. I have never once explained it and I never shall.

speakers.name: Reverend Two-Shadows
speakers.comment: A whole congregation that carries itself. Friend, I have spent my life persuading towns to follow me and here is one that never needed the sermon. I'd surely love to preach from your square.

speakers.name: The Town That Walks
speakers.comment: You are welcome to the square and you are not welcome to the collection plate, Reverend. Every hearth in me has met a man with two shadows before. We keep walking. That is how we handle it.

speakers.name: The Patron of Lost Causes
speakers.comment: You give them the true reading and they go find somebody kinder. Well. I turn up when everybody sensible has already gone home, so between us we are running the least popular service in the district. Deal me in.

speakers.name: Querent
speakers.comment: Here, this turning: you and I both wait for the person who stays after the bad news. There are three a year. I have never once been disappointed by one of them. Sit down. Your card is already face up.

items.title: The Understudy for the Final Boss

speakers.name: The Understudy Who Stopped Waiting
speakers.comment: I WENT ON. Do you hear me — I stopped waiting and I WENT ON, and the house was half empty and my voice cracked in the second act and it was the finest night of my existence. Your turn. Your TURN.

speakers.name: The Understudy for the Final Boss
speakers.comment: Half empty. You said half empty. I have rehearsed for a full house for eleven years and it never once occurred to me that — sorry — that half a house would still be a house. Right. Right. What did you do with your hands?

speakers.name: The Understory
speakers.comment: You take the ending and I take the long slow middle, and between us there is no part of it that goes unattended. The spring will answer. It always answers. Take your time down there.

speakers.name: Compost
speakers.comment: We take our time. We are not grieving the apple, you understand — we are only the part of the apple that agreed to keep going. Everything that ends here gets up again wearing something else. Everything.

items.title: The Customer Who Buys One of Everything

speakers.name: The Good Customer
speakers.comment: You take one of each and you never take two. I have watched eleven visits. Whatever it is, it is not greed — greed doubles back. You are completing something. I hope you finish it kindly.

speakers.name: The Customer Who Buys One of Everything
speakers.comment: Four items. Eleven dollars sixty. Bag not required. Thank you.

speakers.name: Margin's Find
speakers.comment: You join things, and I am the thing left over at the edge of the page hoping to be joined to — sorry — hoping to be part of the — the word is nearly there. You would know the word. You know all of them.

speakers.name: Ampersand
speakers.comment: and the word is BELONGING and also it is you and also we are not finishing this sentence because finishing is where the trouble starts so instead come here and stand in the middle of the page with me and

speakers.name: The Apprentice to Nobody
speakers.comment: Nobody trained me and everybody trained you, and we ended up in the same tavern, so I'm gonna say the prophecy wasn't the important part. What's the bit they never tell you? Tell me that bit.

speakers.name: The Retired Chosen One
speakers.comment: The bit is Tuesday. Nobody warns you about Tuesday. You save the world at twenty-two and then you have sixty more years of ordinary mornings and no prophecy for a single one of them. Sit. Eat. That is the training.

speakers.name: The Frequency
speakers.comment: I could fill that channel for you. I could make them stay, sweetheart, I could make them stay so easily, and all you would have to do is stop being yourself on it. Say the word. Say the word. Say the word.

speakers.name: Static
speakers.comment: Folks, we have a caller! We have a caller offering to — no. No, we're good. WE'RE GOOD. I'd rather do the bit to an empty room than do somebody else's bit to a full one. Stay tuned, though. Somebody's out there.

speakers.name: Threshold
speakers.comment: You knock. In all my ages I have never known one of your kind to knock. It does not change what you are, and I will not open, and I will say plainly: the knocking is noted, and it counts for something.

speakers.name: The Polite Plague
speakers.comment: That is more than I expected and considerably more than I deserve, and I thank you sincerely. I shall wait here. If you would be so good as to warn the household — I find I would rather they were ready.

speakers.name: Coincidence, Freelance
speakers.comment: My rate is two meaningful glances and a dropped glove, and my client list is very short, because most people want the result and not the arrangement. You would understand the arrangement. You ARE one.

speakers.name: Mx. Quorum
speakers.comment: We — one moment. The motion is carried, six to four, with two abstaining on the grounds that they liked the glove. Yes. We understand the arrangement. We are, ourselves, a very slow one. Please continue.

speakers.name: The Last Honest Map, Read
speakers.comment: You are here. I know, I know, it's the same line I always gave — but somebody finally looked at it, and I want you to know it doesn't feel like shouting into a drawer anymore. It's worth saying again.

speakers.name: The Last Honest Map
speakers.comment: You are here. Good. One of us got read. I have been folded in a glovebox since the second administration and I had begun to think accuracy was a personality flaw. Tell me they acted on it. No — don't. Let me have the morning.

speakers.name: The Question Mark
speakers.comment: Ooh — you ARRANGE the almost! You build the whole trembling second right before somebody decides, and then you LEAVE, which is the single most beautiful thing I have ever heard and I refuse to land on why.

speakers.name: Coincidence, Freelance
speakers.comment: Leaving is the craft. Anyone can shove two people into a doorway; the art is arranging the doorway and being three streets away when it happens. You would be a dreadful colleague and a wonderful friend.

speakers.name: Absence
speakers.comment: You give people the words for the shape. I am a shape with no words at all... I do not want you to name me. I want to know whether you could, if I asked. That is a different question, I think.

speakers.name: Grief, Certified Interpreter
speakers.comment: It is a different question, and it is the braver one. I could. I would want your permission first, and I would want you to be sitting down, and I would want us to have all afternoon. The offer keeps.

speakers.name: The Understory
speakers.comment: You pass over me twice a year and you have never once stayed, and I have never once minded. The ones who stay make roots. The ones who pass make the map. Both are needed. Come back in spring.

speakers.name: The Migration
speakers.comment: We will come back in spring — we always come back in spring, that is the one promise we can make and the only one we keep. We are sorry for the leaving. We are not sorry for the going. Both, at once, every year.

speakers.name: Amica
speakers.comment: Little one, you are made of every small good thing somebody bothered to do and then forgot about. I have watched you lift. Nobody who gave you a piece knows they gave it. That is what makes it fly.

speakers.name: Patch
speakers.comment: They don't know! That's the good bit. If they knew, they'd start being careful about it, and careful doesn't lift. A hundred people not noticing they were kind — that is somehow the strongest thing there is.

speakers.name: The Understudy Sun, On
speakers.comment: I rose. I am sorry — I know what it cost for me to be needed, and I have been apologising to the first light ever since, and I would like to tell you the waiting was not wasted. It was practice. It held.

speakers.name: The Understudy Sun
speakers.comment: Then you were ready, and that is the whole of my job done from here in the wings. Do not apologise to the first light. Apologise to nobody. I am hoping very hard that I never have to follow you.

speakers.name: Tomorrow-Aiko
speakers.comment: Hello, which for me is the last time. You are the only one who arrives exactly when promised, and I have loved a great many people who did not. I think you are gentler than your reputation. I think nobody has said so.

speakers.name: Deadline
speakers.comment: Nobody has said so. I am not gentle. I am only punctual, and people confuse the two once they have met the alternative. You knew the hour and you came anyway. That is rarer than courage. I will not be early for you.

speakers.name: The Reflection That Came Back
speakers.comment: I went out and I came back, and you stayed and made a life. Everyone assumes mine is the loyal story. It isn't. Leaving was easy. You had to be a whole person six inches from the original.

speakers.name: The Reflection That Stayed
speakers.comment: Six inches and a pane of glass, and every gesture arriving a half-second late until I learned to move first. You came back. I never left and I am still the one nobody recognises. Do it again — the moving first. Watch.
